summary: This is a clipped Twinkl teaching-resource page explaining cause and effect as an intrinsic relationship where one event brings about another, with examples of single causes with multiple effects. It covers why causality matters for reading and writing stories, predicting outcomes in line with the English national curriculum for KS1, and lists signal words for causes and effects with example sentences. The rest of the page is mostly navigation and promotional listings of teaching resources, which are ignored here.
one_line: A teacher-oriented explanation of cause and effect, its role in reading comprehension and writing, and signal words for causal sentences.
key_facts: Cause and effect is an intrinsic relationship between events and processes, where one causes the other.
A cause-effect relationship is one in which a certain event (the cause) makes another event happen (the effect).
A single cause can have multiple effects.
Cause and effect may also be called causality.
Example: 'I overslept (cause) so I missed my bus (effect).'
Example: 'Your alarm clock makes a loud noise' leads to 'You wake up in time for school.'
Causes listed as signal words include because, because of, since, as a result of, as a consequence of, and now.
Effect signal words listed include so, therefore, consequently, this resulted in, hence, and accordingly.
The national curriculum for English states that children in KS1 should learn to 'predict what might happen on the basis of what has been read so far'.
The note states that without a cause, the text would be stagnant and nothing more would happen.
Causality allows us to logically explain events and helps us to solve problems and provide reasoning for why something happened.
When children write, they should connect their ideas by using the concept of cause and effect.
Twinkl's 'Pip Predicts' Early Predictions Activity Pack uses Predicting Pip from the Totally Pawsome Reading Gang.
The KS1 Predicting Pip pack includes SATs-style questions to help year 2 prepare for their exams, plus four short stories.
The Cause and Effect Scenarios PowerPoint features a range of scenarios for children to identify causes and effects.
